title: Autoscaler flapping after memory-metric mismatch and KEDA scale-to-zero interplay
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: During a regional capacity event on 2025-02-14 we observed repeated autoscaler "flapping" in the inference API fleet for hosted customers. Pods were rapidly scaled down to zero by KEDA and then overscaled on traffic spikes, causing long cold-start tail latency and temporary quota exhaustion in the scheduler. This incident led to elevated API error rates and a measurable increase in P99 latency for 47 minutes during peak traffic.
timeline: 2025-02-14T10:12Z - first alert (increased P95/P99). 2025-02-14T10:20Z - automated scaling down observed in control plane logs. 2025-02-14T10:27Z - surge of new pods and scheduler throttling. 2025-02-14T10:35Z - mitigation: temporarily disabled scale-to-zero for impacted deployment and bumped minReplicas to 2. 2025-02-14T10:59Z - traffic stabilized and error rates fell. 2025-02-14T12:00Z - full post-incident triage kicked off.
detection: Primary signal was P99 latency + 5xx rate (>0.8%) from the Redwood API synthetic monitors and customer dashboards. PagerDuty alert routed to on-call infra engineer. Secondary indicators: KEDA scaler events showing scale-down to zero within 30s of low qps and memory metric resets recorded in Prometheus.
mitigation: 1) Disabled KEDA scale-to-zero for the affected Deployment. 2) Increased HPA minReplicas to 2 for the service as an immediate stop-gap. 3) Reverted a recent config change that reduced HPA stabilization window. 4) Cold-start optimized container image pulled to warm caches in a canary group.
root_cause: A metric mismatch and a recent config change combined to create an unstable downscale loop. KEDA was configured to use a Prometheus query that returned instance RSS memory which resets on GC, producing transient low values. Separately, a change in runtime-1.20 removed a conservative downscale stabilization window (intended to be temporary) which made HPA/KEDA more aggressive. The two combined: KEDA rapidly scaled to zero on short-lived low-memory samples, then traffic spikes required full cold starts causing upstream scheduler queueing and apparent capacity exhaustion.
contributing_factors: 1) Prometheus query used for KEDA scaler referenced process_resident_memory_bytes instead of application_heap_bytes. 2) Runtime change in 1.20.2 to the autoscaler stabilization window made downscales immediate. 3) Insufficient warm pool (minReplicas=0) for latency-sensitive endpoints. 4) Lack of end-to-end test simulating GC cycles + sudden traffic bursts. 5) Monitoring alert thresholds were tied to aggregate error rate and not to scaling churn metrics.
impact_summary: 47 minutes of elevated error rate and P99 latency for the inference /generate endpoint in us-west-2, affecting ~12% of production traffic for hosted customers. No data loss. Two paying customers reported user-facing timeouts during the event window.

postmortem_summary: The outage was caused by an interaction between an aggressive autoscaler downscale policy and a noisy memory metric that produced false low readings. That combination allowed KEDA to rapidly scale pods to zero and removed the warm pool necessary for latency-sensitive workloads. We mitigated the event within an hour and implemented a sequence of fixes: metric query hardening, reinstating stabilization windows, minimum warm pool policy, and improved testing and observability to detect scaler churn earlier. Long-term work includes capacity exercises and autoscaler policy tuning across releases.
follow_up_notes:
- Verify other services using process-level memory metrics and migrate them to application-level metrics where appropriate.
- Consider an autoscaler abstraction that combines multiple signals (qps, heap, latency) with voting to avoid single-metric flaps.
- Schedule a cross-team retro with SRE, Infra, Runtime, and Product to align SLA expectations and rollout cadence for autoscaler changes.
notes_for_pm_and_design: PMs: update customer-facing KB about scale-to-zero behavior and recommended configurations for latency-sensitive endpoints. Design: prepare a brief for console UX to surface scaler health and warm-pool recommendations on the Deployment settings panel.
